name: Ohio
agency: Ohio Bureau of Motor Vehicles (Ohio Department of Public Safety)
permitAge: 15 and a half (vision screening and knowledge test at 15 years 6 months; temporary instruction permit identification card (TIPIC) bought within 60 days of passing; valid one year, ORC 4507.05)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours logged with an eligible licensed driver, including at least 10 at night; notarized BMV 5791 Fifty-Hour Affidavit signed by a parent, guardian, custodian or adult in loco parentis (Ohio Driver Manual, Sections 1 and 12)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months (under 18 only; ORC 4507.071, Ohio Driver Manual Section 1)
teen.nightLimit: Probationary license under 18: first 12 months no driving midnight to 6 a.m.; after 12 months 1 a.m. to 5 a.m.; unless with a parent or guardian, or driving to or from work (employer form BMV 2825) or a school or religious event (BMV 2826) (Ohio Driver Manual Section 12)
teen.passengerLimit: First 12 months of probationary license: no more than one non-family passenger unless a parent or guardian is along (Ohio Driver Manual Section 12)
teen.phone: Adults: holding or supporting a phone is illegal in most cases and a primary offense; only a single touch or swipe; 1st offense in two years 2 points and up to $150 (a distracted driving course can avoid fine and points), 2nd 3 points and up to $250, 3rd 4 points, up to $500, possible 90-day suspension; doubled in work zones. Under 18 (and permit holders): no device use at all, even hands-free, except navigation or emergency calls; 1st violation 60-day suspension and $150 (Ohio Driver Manual Section 3)

notes: Handbook: Ohio Driver Manual (Digest of Motor Vehicle Laws), official online HTML manual in 13 sections on publicsafety.ohio.gov, each section dated January 26, 2024. No PDF and no page numbers, so questions carry page null and the section URL in src. Read in full 2026-10-09.
Knowledge test: 40 multiple-choice questions, 75 percent to pass; minimum age 15 years 6 months; wait one day after a failure; online testing allows two attempts in six months (Section 1).

Test languages: ASL, Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Haitian Creole, Japanese, Russian, Somali, Spanish; own interpreter for other languages at a Driver Exam Station (Section 1). No official Spanish manual found.

Permit supervision: under 16 a parent, guardian, custodian, licensed instructor or adult 21+ in loco parentis in the front seat; 16-17 any licensed driver 21+ in the front passenger seat, but midnight to 6 a.m. only with a licensed parent, guardian or custodian; 18+ a licensed driver 21+ (Section 1).
Driver education under 21: 24 hours classroom or online plus 8 hours with a driving school (Section 1).

Move over (ORC 4511.213, Section 9): applies to stopped police, emergency, road service (tow, snowplow), waste collection, highway maintenance and PUCO inspection vehicles with warning lights on; not to every vehicle with flashing lights.
School bus (ORC 4511.75, Section 5): fewer than four lanes, all traffic stops at least 10 feet away; four or more lanes, only traffic going the same direction as the bus.
SB 419 (136th GA) would lower the permit age to 15 and lengthen the holding period to one year; status unknown, so not used in questions.
HB 616 (136th GA) would require every test language; status unknown.
